step1_analysis.description: A series sense amplifier featuring a cross-coupled NMOS pair and clocked tail transistors. It samples and amplifies small differential input signals into full-swing digital outputs during the clock's evaluation phase, commonly used in high-speed transceivers for data recovery.

paper_reference.title: A 2.5–10-Gb/s CMOS Transceiver With Alternating Edge-Sampling Phase Detection for Loop Characteristic Stabilization

delay_clk_to_out.description: Time delay from the rising edge of the clock to the output resolving its state.

sky130_expected.calculation: Discharge of 10fF load through tail NMOS. I_tail ≈ 0.5 * 270u * 10 * (1.8-0.42)^2 ≈ 2.5mA. dV/dt = 2.5mA / 10fF = 250 V/ns. Time to cross threshold is roughly 5-10ps, plus intrinsic gate delays.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted for SKY130 1.8V process. The strong tail current provides very fast evaluation, but parasitic capacitances will limit the minimum delay.

power_avg.description: Average power consumption of the sense amplifier during active clocking.

sky130_expected.calculation: Static current exists because input PMOS remains partially ON. Vsg = 0.85V -> I_static ≈ 45µA. Dynamic power for 10fF at 1GHz ≈ 32µW. Total power ≈ 1.8V * 45µA + 32µW ≈ 113µW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports total transceiver power. A single sense amplifier block consumes a small fraction of this, typically in the hundreds of microwatts.

voltage_swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage difference between the high and low states of the output.

sky130_expected.calculation: High state is pulled to VDD (1.8V) by PMOS. Low state is pulled to GND by strong cross-coupled NMOS fighting a weak PMOS, settling near ~50mV. Swing ≈ 1.8V - 0.05V = 1.75V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: While the paper mentions 800mV (likely for CML logic parts), this specific CMOS latch topology will swing nearly rail-to-rail in SKY130 at 1.8V.

step3_testbench.description: Transient testbench to measure clock-to-Q delay, voltage swing, and average power consumption of the sense amplifier under a small differential input.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Sense Amplifier Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u
.param W_xm7=5u L_xm7=0.5u
.param W_xm8=5u L_xm8=0.5u
.param W_xm9=5u L_xm9=0.5u
.param W_xm10=5u L_xm10=0.5u
.param W_xm11=5u L_xm11=0.5u

* Supplies and Bias
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 0.9
VLABEL_NET_1 LABEL_NET_1 0 0.9
VLABEL_NET_2 LABEL_NET_2 0 0.9

* Inputs (Small differential signal around 0.9V common mode)
VINP N0 0 0.95
VINN N1 0 0.85

* Clock Signal (1 GHz)
VCLK N3 0 PULSE(0 1.8 200p 20p 20p 400p 1000p)

* DUT
XM1 N5 N1 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N6 N3 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N2 N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 N4 N3 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 N4 LABEL_NET_0 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 N5 N1 N6 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}
XM7 N6 LABEL_NET_1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm7} w={W_xm7}
XM8 N5 N2 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm8} w={W_xm8}
XM9 N2 N0 N4 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm9} w={W_xm9}
XM10 N2 N5 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm10} w={W_xm10}
XM11 N6 LABEL_NET_2 N4 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm11} w={W_xm11}

* Load Capacitances
C1 N2 0 10f
C2 N5 0 10f

.control
tran 1p 2000p

* Measure Delays
meas tran delay_clk_to_outn trig v(N3) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(N2) val=0.45 fall=1
meas tran delay_clk_to_outp trig v(N3) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(N5) val=1.35 rise=1

* Measure Voltage Swing
meas tran v_outn_min min v(N2)
meas tran v_outp_max max v(N5)
let swing = v_outp_max - v_outn_min
print swing

* Measure Power
meas tran power_avg avg i(VVDD)
let power_mw = -power_avg * 1.8 * 1000
print power_mw

quit
.endc
.end
